I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over thirty years. My children moved to the city. My husband does occasional wage work, but the fields are mostly my responsibility now. I have about 10 mu of flat, loamy land. I know what this land wants.

**My thinking:**

Everyone here grows wheat and maize in rotation — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same fields. I've done it this way my whole life and so has everyone on my street. The grain station buys it reliably, and I know the inputs. There's no reason to change.

For wheat, I already sowed it last October. Now I need to manage it through to June harvest — topdressing nitrogen at jointing, watering before heading, watching for aphids and rust. I use the Jimai seeds from the village supply co-op, not the old varieties anymore, because yields are clearly better.

For summer maize after wheat harvest, I'll seed straight into the stubble without ploughing — saves fuel and the village agricultural technician said it helps the soil. I use Xianyu hybrid seed, everyone does, it's strong and high-yielding.

I keep 2 mu near the house for garlic and vegetables. I sell some garlic locally in spring and we eat the vegetables ourselves. It doesn't need much.

I'll water wheat four times — before winter, at turning green, jointing, and heading. Maize I water at sowing and again at silking if rain is short. Fertilizer I apply as I always have, a bit extra nitrogen never hurt in my experience, though my son told me I use too much.
